member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeLogAbi
member.summary: ADR-081 log mailbox PODs for the log_* root slots. The mailbox itself lives in NativeCore lumio-diagnostics and the record is defined in lumio-kernel, where its size and every offset are pinned by const assertions; this section mirrors that struct field for field, and sdk-native re-asserts the equality at compile time, so the two can never drift apart quietly. These are the fixed-width shapes that cross the ABI. Records are fixed width by ADR-081 decision 6 - no pointers, no owned allocations, no variable-length tail - so a drain writes straight into a caller-owned array and the payload is bounded at LOG_TEXT_CAPACITY bytes with a truncation flag rather than a silent drop. Message template, target and file:line are NOT in the record: they are interned per callsite and fetched once through log_callsite_lookup, so the hot path never formats a string. Audit, TxnJournal, CommandLog and Failure Bundle do not travel here (ADR-011 / ADR-032).

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeLogLevel
member.summary: The single level scale for both languages, one byte wide because that is how the kernel stores it. Rust tracing maps one-to-one. Microsoft.Extensions.Logging maps Trace/Debug/Information/Warning/Error one-to-one and folds Critical into Error. There is no Off: the kernel Level enum stops at Error, so LogLevel.None has no counterpart here and is never pushed through log_configure - a managed host that wants silence mutes its own provider. A record carrying a level this build cannot name is treated as Error rather than dropped, so an unknown value is a reason to look, not a reason to lose the line.

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeLogLang

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeLogFieldKind
member.summary: How to reinterpret the 8 raw bytes of log_field.value; the vocabulary is the kernel's FIELD_KIND_* constants, value for value. None means the slot carries nothing. I64 is a two's-complement bit cast, U64 the raw integer, F64 an IEEE-754 bit cast, Bool 0 or 1. Text means the value was textual and was rendered into the bounded payload instead - the record itself never carries a string.

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeLogField
member.summary: 16-byte numeric field (4 bytes of tail padding after kind). name_id 0 is unnamed; every other value is read in the producer's own namespace, which lang selects. For lang=Rust it is the mailbox-interned field-name id (1-based, assigned in first-seen order by the kernel name table) and is resolvable only inside the process that interned it - no ABI slot resolves it today, so a managed drain pump reports the id, never a made-up name. For lang=CSharp it is the managed convention: 1 is the Microsoft.Extensions.Logging EventId.Id and other values are unassigned. kind selects how value is read.

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeLogRecord
member.summary: 416-byte fixed-width record, 8-byte aligned. This is the byte-for-byte shape of the kernel's LogRecord (NativeCore lumio-kernel log::record, const-asserted there); the ABI describes that struct and does not get to invent its own order or widths. seq is the mailbox-assigned monotonically increasing publication sequence; refused attempts do not consume a sequence number and are reported by mailbox counters. unix_micros is UTC microseconds since the epoch, 0 where the target has no wall clock (wasm32). tick and world come from the innermost span (Rust info_span!) or ILogger.BeginScope (C#) and are 0 when absent - never fabricated (ADR-081 decision 5). callsite_id resolves through log_callsite_lookup and is 0 for records pushed by log_emit. flags is a bit set of LOG_FLAG_TRUNCATED (1, the payload was cut) and LOG_FLAG_FIELDS_TRUNCATED (2, more fields were offered than LOG_FIELD_CAPACITY); every other bit must be zero. field_count is at most LOG_FIELD_CAPACITY and text_len at most LOG_TEXT_CAPACITY - a reader clamps both rather than trusting a foreign producer. text holds text_len bytes of UTF-8; the tail beyond text_len is zero-filled and must not be read.

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeLogCounters
member.summary: 24-byte process-lifetime monotonic totals. accepted + dropped_full equals every emit attempt: a producer is never blocked, so a full mailbox drops and counts (ADR-081 failure semantics 1). truncated counts records whose payload exceeded LOG_TEXT_CAPACITY.

member.name: F:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.PredictionAbi.PredictionDataUnavailable

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeBase64Encoder
member.summary: Standard Base64 through the native codec_base64_encode_v1 root slot (ADR-122). The slot forwards NativeCore lumio_codec::base64_encode_into, the engine's only Base64 encoder: RFC 4648 §4 alphabet (A–Z a–z 0–9 + /), = padding, no line breaks. For the same bytes the result equals character for character.

remarks.para: Why not : on the managed Tick path its vectorized CoreLib implementation is compiled on first use, so the first Tick paid JIT that steady state never pays (ADR-118 decision 5). Here the Tick path runs only this facade's own methods, which the Runtime Prime warm-up compiles ahead of time, plus one unmanaged call.

The slot is called through an unmanaged function pointer with blittable arguments: no marshalling delegate, no managed allocation for . Every native call goes through one non-inlined method, and makes one empty-input call through it, so whatever one-time transition code the runtime needs for that call is prepared when the encoder is created, not inside a Tick.
Instances are immutable and hold no native state: share one across threads freely. Calls throw once the lease that created the encoder is disposed.
